name: Freight consignments and shipping documentation
one_line: The custody record for one consignment moving from a consignor through a carrier to a consignee: booking and waybill identity, packages and goods, origin and destination, customs or transport controls, handover, delivery and loss/damage exceptions. A purchase order, address, tracking number, invoice, packing image or carrier brand is not enough without the custody and handover relation. Placeholder template: the logistics schema remains field-less pending R1c.

deterministic: a consignment note, waybill or CMR structure joining consignor/shipper, consignee and carrier roles to one goods description, package count or weight, place of taking over, place of delivery and carrier or receiver acknowledgement

a bill of lading or sea/air waybill structure joining shipper, consignee or notify party, vessel/voyage or flight, container and seal identifiers, cargo description, origin/destination and condition or endorsement sections

a packing-list structure whose rows are packages, cartons or pallets with marks and numbers, contents, quantity, net/gross weight and dimensions, with no unit price, tax treatment or amount due as its central structure

a proof-of-delivery structure pairing a consignment or shipment reference with delivered-at time/place, receiving signature or scan event, delivery status and shortage, damage, refusal or carded exception

a customs or export declaration joining movement/declaration reference, declarant or representative, commodity classification, origin, procedure, value or incoterm, package/goods lines and customs submission or release state

a transport exception or carrier-claim packet joining consignment identity to loss, damage, delay or shortage narrative, inspection evidence, seal/condition observations, claimant, correspondence and settlement or recovery status

a carrier integration or EDI payload whose segments join shipment/consignment, party-role qualifiers, package or unit counts and status events such as booked, collected, in transit, held, delivered or refused

an email whose native sender/recipient/subject fields cite a consignment, booking, container or waybill and whose body or attachment structure includes custody parties, goods, handover, delivery or exception evidence

an archive manifest linking one consignment/container across booking, commercial invoice, packing list, waybill, customs declaration, origin certificate and proof of delivery; manifest evidence does not donate facts to members
a multimodal handover record joining one shipment to rail, road, sea or air legs, each carrier or custody event, package/container identity and receipt or exception state
a delivery-point photograph or scan only when its own submission record joins visible goods/seal/receipt evidence to a consignment and delivery event; an image alone remains Photos or Review Later

template.why: The logistics schema declares no legal fields under PR-6, so this template does not write consignment, carrier, asset, site or record_type dimensions. Conditional on R1c promoting the schema proposals, the useful projection is custody context or carrier only where it genuinely separates the corpus -> consignment/container -> record_type, with site/depot or asset/vehicle branches only in their respective warehouse/fleet situations. Consignee names and delivery addresses are role-bearing evidence, not default folder dimensions; carrier is a counterparty and should not become a collector folder by default. The schema's default is distinct from this row because this template is one movement's custody dossier across heterogeneous documents, not a general logistics branch. It is not time-first: 00 says, "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." No executable dimension is claimed until R1c licenses a canonical key.

collides_with.signal: SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Packing-List_PO-7714.xlsx. Logistics wins when the same bytes establish package-level custody, carrier handover, origin/destination and movement; business_operations.procurement-sourcing wins when they are sourcing or purchase support for a supplier award, and neither side may treat a purchase-order reference as a consignment or completed delivery.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Packing-List_PO-7714.xlsx. Logistics wins for the carrier's package and custody chain; retail_hospitality.supplier-order wins for a retailer/hospitality buyer's supplier order, expected goods and replenishment workflow, and a packing list alone does not decide whether it is a shipment document or an order member.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Goods-Received_NCR-118.pdf. Logistics wins when the same bytes prove carrier handover, packages, condition in transit or delivery exception; manufacturing.production-record wins when they record received product/lot disposition in a production-control workflow, and a consignment reference does not convert an incoming-quality decision into a delivery event.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Fish-Transport-Document_Lot-L-771.pdf. Logistics wins for post-landing vehicle, seal, destination and consignment custody; resource_operations.fisheries-catch wins when the same bytes are retained in the originating vessel/trip/landing/catch reconciliation, and transported product weight is not silently rewritten as catch.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Driver-Run-Sheet_2026-04-11.ics. Logistics.shipment wins when the same bytes are tied to a consignment's actual collection/delivery and custody events; logistics.route-dispatch wins when they are a working-day plan of vehicle, driver, ordered stops and planned-versus-actual run performance, and a calendar booking alone proves neither completed shipment nor route execution.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: POD_Consignment-CN-4021.jpg. Logistics.shipment wins when the image is evidence in the whole consignment across origin, carrier and destination; logistics.last-mile-pod wins when its decisive role is doorstep delivery proof, recipient/attempt status and final-mile exception, and camera location or signature alone cannot establish either custody scope.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Export-Declaration_MRN-7781.xml. Logistics.shipment wins when the declaration is one member of a goods movement and carrier handover dossier; logistics.customs-export wins when its central function is customs/export filing, classification, declarant and release/compliance status, and a movement reference alone does not establish physical delivery.

SAME FIXTURE BYTES: Driver-Run-Sheet_2026-04-11.ics. Logistics.shipment wins for the consignment/drop sequence and goods custody; logistics.fleet-vehicle wins for the vehicle's identity, licensing, inspection, maintenance or operator records, and a vehicle or driver name in a route plan does not establish a fleet lifecycle record.

sensitivity_why: Consignment contents, addresses, delivery schedules, recipient names, driver or vehicle identifiers, customs values, seal numbers, route history, claims and commercial terms can expose personal delivery patterns, business operations or security-sensitive movement. This row assigns no handling class; P7's file-level classification and local/cloud policy remain authoritative.
open_question: NJ-LOG-SHIP-1: R1c must decide whether this template reuses logistics proposals `consignment`, `carrier`, `asset`, `site` and `record_type`, and whether carrier is destination-eligible or only a role/search facet. NJ-LOG-SHIP-2: Should one package/consignment dossier remain distinct from last-mile POD, customs-export and route-dispatch siblings when the same submitted bytes occur in all workflows, or should custody role select one mutex template? NJ-LOG-SHIP-3: Goods-received and packing-list files can support Manufacturing, Retail/Hospitality and Business Operations as well as Logistics; should P9 represent that coactivation, or does custody ownership require an explicit user decision? This template deliberately authors no also_holds_with edge. NJ-LOG-SHIP-4: R2/R4 must settle deployment-specific consignment, container, vehicle, customs and carrier identifiers; no regex, jurisdiction, tariff rule or legal threshold is asserted here.
